public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 155

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/155](https://www.erdosproblems.com/155)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos155

/--
Let $F(N)$ be the size of the largest Sidon subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$.
-/
noncomputable abbrev F (N : ℕ) : ℕ := Finset.maxSidonSubsetCard (Finset.Icc 1 N)

/--
Is it true that for every $k \geq 1$ we have
$$
F(N + k) \leq F(N) + 1
$$
for all sufficiently large $N$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_155 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, F (N + k) ≤ F N + 1 := by
  sorry

-- TODO: This may even hold with $k \approx ε * N ^ (1 / 2)$.

end Erdos155

review.notes:
No findings. Erdos155.erdos_155 matches both erdosproblems.com/155 and Erdős's primary statement in [Er92c] word for word: for every k ≥ 1 there is N₀(k) with F(N+k) ≤ F(N)+1 for all N ≥ N₀(k).

Erdos155.F is the standard maximum Sidon-subset size of {1,…,N}. It uses the same convention as Erdős 30. Its `#eval` values for N = 0..13 match OEIS A143824.

Erdős's f(n) counts sequences a_1<…<a_k ≤ n. If that were read as allowing 0, it would only shift N by one, because the Sidon property is translation invariant. The claim is about all sufficiently large N, so the shift does not matter. In any case erdosproblems.com fixes {1,…,N}, which is exactly what the Lean uses.

In the default `answer` mode, `#check` shows the slot as `True ↔ …`. That is the repository's documented convention, not a defect.

The stronger variant ("may even hold with k ≈ εN^{1/2}", Erdős's (10)) is not formalized. It appears only as a TODO comment. That is an omission, not a misformalization.

I could not access the full texts of [ESS94] (ScienceDirect blocked) or [Er94b] (not in the Rényi archive, which stops at 1990). They are secondary citations of the same conjecture and do not affect the verdict. The status (`research open`) matches erdosproblems.com ("OPEN") and the teorth database ("open").
